summary: The dominant market-relevant development in this window is the escalation of US-China trade tensions: President Trump threatened to raise tariffs on Chinese goods, causing Chinese stocks to fall more than 5% and US stock futures to drop sharply, while the planned trade negotiations were thrown into doubt.
mechanism: Renewed tariff threats and the resulting uncertainty over whether a US-China trade deal would proceed directly hit equity markets in both countries, producing a sharp sell-off in Chinese stocks and a decline in US futures, which is a classic transmission channel for a spike in price volatility.

claims.claim: Chinese stocks fell more than 5% intraday following Trump's tariff threats.
Planned US-China trade negotiations were put in question as a result of the tariff threats.
US stock futures also fell sharply in reaction to the same news.
Separately, the US deployed a carrier strike group and bomber task force to the Middle East citing threats from Iran, adding geopolitical risk during the same window.

competing_explanation: The US military buildup against Iran (carrier strike group and bomber deployment) could independently have raised geopolitical risk premiums and contributed to volatility, separate from or alongside the trade tension story.
